commit_message:
fix(session): sequence worktree discard after PTY reap on explicit removal

discardWorktree() ran before destroy(), while the PTY still held the worktree as its cwd on Windows. git worktree remove --force failed under that directory lock, leaking the worktree and its checked-out branch, so the follow-up branch -D also failed and a same-named re-add hit "session branch already checked out". Discard now runs after destroy() kills the PTY and its reap settles.

Constraint: git worktree remove --force cannot run while a live process holds the worktree as its cwd on Windows (directory lock)
Confidence: medium
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: no test run confirming session removal no longer leaks worktree/branch on Windows

findings.issue: backend.js reaches into sess._killReap, a private/internal Session field, directly from outside the Session class instead of exposing a public method (e.g. sess.whenKilled() or similar). Couples backend.js to Session's internal implementation detail.

Fix assumes a property named sess._killReap holds the PTY kill/reap promise. If sessions.js actually exposes this under a different name (e.g. a reap promise set inside destroy()), Promise.resolve(sess._killReap) resolves immediately with undefined and discardWorktree runs right after destroy() with no delay, silently reintroducing the exact race (worktree still held by cwd) this diff is meant to fix.
findings.fix: Confirm sess._killReap is set synchronously inside Session.destroy() in session/sessions.js and actually resolves only after the PTY process exit/reap completes.

findings.issue: sessions.delete(id) fires immediately, before the chained discardWorktree completes. A same-named session re-added quickly, before the deferred worktree/branch removal settles, can still hit the 'branch already checked out' failure the comment describes, just in a narrower window.
findings.fix: If this matters in practice, await the discardWorktree chain (or track pending discards) before allowing a same-name re-add, or document the narrowed race as acceptable.

historical.message:
fix(session): tear down worktree after PTY reap on quick delete

Quick delete fired sess.discardWorktree() unawaited and BEFORE
sess.destroy() killed the PTY. On Windows `git worktree remove --force`
fails while the live claude/conhost process still holds the worktree as
its cwd (directory lock); the swallowed failure leaked the worktree, and
the follow-up `branch -D` then failed too (branch still checked out), so
a same-named re-add hit "session branch already checked out; running in
place". Destroy first, then discard only after the _killReap promise
settles, so removal runs on a dead process and drops both worktree and
branch cleanly.

Constraint: _teardownSession stays sync (called from a sync reload loop); discard is deferred fire-and-forget, ordered via the reap promise.
Rejected: awaiting discard inline (would make teardown async across all callers); killing PTY inside discardWorktree (couples an operator action to the teardown path).
Directive: Explicit removal throws the worktree away; shutdown/restart still skip discard so pending-review worktrees survive the next-boot reconcile.
Confidence: high
Scope-risk: narrow
Not-tested: live Windows quick-delete + same-name re-add (verified by root-cause reasoning + existing teardown/kill suites, 50 pass)
